title: Nanopillar metasurfaces uniting high optical reflectivity with ultracoherent nanomechanics
abstract: Mechanically compliant mirrors are key components in cavity optomechanics. However, the requirements to achieve the best optical and mechanical performance are usually in direct competition. A high reflectivity for tightly focused beams entails thick reflectors, whereas ultracoherent flexural nanomechanics necessitates thin membranes. We eliminate this trade-off by introducing high-refractive-index nanopillar metasurfaces on top of a thin membrane. We pattern a 50 micrometer-diameter array of nanopillars to form a photonic crystal. The flat band behavior of guided resonances in the photonic crystal enables a reflectivity of 99.82(1)% for a tightly focused beam of 7 micrometer waist. The combination of two guided resonances creates a 100 nanometer-wide high-reflectivity band around 1550 nanometer. Simultaneously, the nanopillar patterning realizes a density-modulated phononic crystal that isolates an ultracoherent localized mechanical mode with a $Q\cdot f$-product of $2\cdot 10^{14}$Hz. The demonstrated nanopillar metasurfaces enable lightweight mirrors for room-temperature quantum optomechanics and for use as levitated mirrors or lightsails.
comment: 9 pages, 4 figures; incl supporting information of 29 pages

bite.hook: Nanopillar metasurface hits 99.82% reflectivity for focused beams alongside a 2×10¹⁴ Hz mechanical Q·f product.
tldr: Overcame the trade-off between thick high-reflectivity optics and thin mechanical resonators in optomechanics.
Patterned a 50 µm array of high-index nanopillars on a thin membrane to create dual guided resonances.
Achieved 99.82% reflectivity for a 7 µm waist at 1550 nm and a phononic Q·f product of 2×10¹⁴ Hz.
bite.whyItMatters: Cavity optomechanics requires mirrors that are both ultralight and exceptionally reflective, which usually conflict physically. Solving this trade-off paves the way for room-temperature quantum sensors, levitated optomechanics, and miniature lightsails.
bite.eli5: Normally, light bounces best off thick, heavy mirrors, but delicate quantum experiments need mirrors as light as soap bubbles. By carving microscopic pillars into a thin film, researchers built a featherweight mirror that reflects almost all laser light.

glossary.shortDef: The study of interactions between light trapped in an optical cavity and mechanical motion.
glossary.eli5Def: Bouncing laser light off tiny vibrating mirrors to study how light pressure and motion interact.

glossary.shortDef: A periodic optical nanostructure designed to manipulate and guide specific wavelengths of light.
glossary.eli5Def: A material patterned with tiny, repeating structures that act like traffic lanes for light.

glossary.shortDef: A localized optical mode trapped inside a slab that couples constructively to external radiation.
glossary.eli5Def: A trapped pocket of light that catches incoming laser rays and reflects them strongly back out.

glossary.shortDef: The product of mechanical quality factor and frequency, measuring thermal isolation.
glossary.eli5Def: A figure of merit measuring how long a tiny resonator can vibrate before losing its energy to heat.
